Question 10 of 11 · The Quran

The Quran's literary challenge

Short answer

It challenges anyone who doubts it to produce one chapter like it. The challenge still stands.

Source: Quran 2:23 (opens in a new tab)

The evidence

The Quran challenges anyone who doubts it to produce one chapter like it.

The challenge is still open.

Why this is significant

Poetry was part of public life in pre-Islamic Arabia. In Britannica’s words, the poet was “a major verbal weapon.” The Quran was revealed in that setting, in their own language, and it challenged them directly:

وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِّن مِّثْلِهِ وَادْعُوا شُهَدَاءَكُم مِّن دُونِ اللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ

“And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to Our servant, then produce a sûrah like it and call your helpers other than Allah, if what you say is true.”

Quran 2:23

If anyone had met it, the challenge would have ended there.

Objections

You might say“Literary quality is subjective”

Our answer

The challenge is more specific than style.

More than beauty

The challenge is to produce one chapter like the Quran’s. Its shortest chapter, Al-Kawthar, has just three verses. If this were only a matter of style, one short chapter should be easy to match.
